key_insight: Inter-Stance introduces a publicly available dyadic multimodal corpus that links synchronized video, audio, transcripts and participant self-reports to enable fine-grained conversational stance analysis between interacting partners.
problem_solved: Addresses the absence of datasets that capture both multimodal behavioral signals and self-reported appraisals from multiple people in natural dyadic interaction, which has limited study and modeling of interpersonal stance, alignment, and moment-to-moment social evaluation.
method: Recorded naturalistic dyadic conversations with synchronized multimodal streams (video, audio, transcripts) and post‑interaction self‑report measures from each participant.
Annotated interactional stance and related social signals (e.g., alignment, mimicry, affective cues) and packaged standardized labels and metadata for use in supervised evaluation.
Provided benchmark tasks and evaluation protocols (stance classification, temporal alignment, cross‑modal fusion) with baseline model results to demonstrate utility.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to train and evaluate models that reason about interpersonal stance and social dynamics across modalities, improving conversational agents, social-signal understanding, and research on human-human and human-AI interaction.

paper_title: Inter-Stance: A Dyadic Multimodal Corpus for Conversational Stance Analysis
paper_authors: Xiang Zhang, Xiaotian Li, Taoyue Wang, Nan Bi, Xin Zhou
